currentContext.strengths: Multi-disciplinary engineering base across seven infrastructure verticals reduces dependence on any single sector|Pan-India presence with long-standing relationships with public and private sector clients|Diversified order book (`83,004 crore consolidated, FY26) balancing sectoral risk|Project management systems, equipment base and skilled workforce built over four decades of execution experience|Disciplined bidding and selective project selection prioritising execution capability and revenue visibility over speculative growth
currentContext.strategies: Selective, disciplined bidding — prioritise projects that match execution capability, offer revenue visibility and a balanced risk-return profile, avoiding speculative growth|Protect project-level economics and margins across market cycles rather than chase scale|Strengthen working capital management: collections, cash conversion and procurement planning|Strengthen digital project controls, project monitoring systems and risk-based decision-making|Maintain a diversified, multi-vertical portfolio (Buildings, Transportation, Water & Environment, Electrical T&D, Irrigation, Railways, Mining) to reduce dependence on any single segment|Focus on converting the order book into revenue, margins and cash flow through execution-led, sustainable value creation|The AGM notice includes declaration of a `2.20/share dividend for FY26 as recommended by the Board. The Company maintains long-term bank facility ratings of CARE AA-/Stable (reaffirmed December 2025, with an enhanced facility of `21,287 crore) and India Ratings IND AA-/Stable, alongside short-term ratings of CARE A1+, indicating a stable credit profile underpinning its capital allocation. Unclaimed dividends are transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund after seven years per statutory requirement, with `7,20,960 transferred in FY26 relating to the 2017-18 final dividend.
currentContext.expansion: As an EPC/construction contractor, NCC's 'expansion' is expressed through the scale and mix of client-awarded projects under execution rather than owned-plant capex. In Water & Environment, ongoing projects include the Multigroup Village Water Supply Scheme Firozabad Pkg-1 (Uttar Pradesh, raw water intake 586 MLD and WTPs of 456 MLD serving ~780 villages), Water Supply Scheme Agra Pkg-1 (17 Clear Water Reservoirs of 14,975 KL capacity serving 899 villages), Patwadh Water Supply Scheme (120 MLD water treatment plant with associated pipelines) and the Kasara Dantiwada Lift Irrigation scheme in Gujarat (MS pipeline exceeding 200 km connecting 159 ponds across 60 villages, irrigating 7,500 hectares). In Irrigation, major FY26 projects include the Barnar Reservoir in Bihar (~2.83 TMC capacity, primarily agricultural/groundwater recharge) and the Palamuru Reservoir in Telangana (part of the Palamuru-Rangaredy Lift Irrigation Scheme, gross capacity 16.4 TMC, with an expansive bund stretching ~15.23 km), plus the Punganur Branch Canal in Rayalseema, Andhra Pradesh. In Electrical (T&D), FY26 major projects span High Voltage 400/220 kV AIS/GIS substations for State DISCOMs in Karnataka and Telangana, distribution-line and system-improvement upgrades across Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Jharkhand, distribution automation and underground cabling for BESCOM in Karnataka, smart prepaid metering for State DISCOMs in North Bihar and Maharashtra, and optical fibre network build-out for BSNL in Madhya Pradesh and Uttarakhand connecting Gram Panchayats and villages.

risks.risk: Working capital risk from project delays and delayed collections
risks.note: Project delays, cost overruns and delayed collections increase working capital requirements, leading to higher borrowings and finance costs; the debt-equity ratio rose 43% YoY (0.21x to 0.30x) in FY26 due to high utilisation of borrowings from low collections from customers.

risks.risk: Political and regulatory risk across multiple states
risks.note: Operations across multiple states expose the Company to varied administrative and policy conditions, which can cause clearance delays, project disruptions or contractual uncertainties.

risks.risk: Competition risk in niche project segments
risks.note: An increase in operators in niche project segments creates pressure on pricing and margins.
Complex project requirements involving subcontractors, vendors, designs, right-of-way and mobilisation can lead to delays, cost overruns and execution inefficiencies.
A competitive bidding environment can lead to disputes and claims, resulting in litigation, delayed recoveries and margin pressure.
Order wins depend on states, departments and sectoral opportunities, exposing the Company to volatility in order inflow.
Geopolitical volatility and input-availability concerns can cause procurement delays and cost volatility.
Heavy rains, changing weather patterns and water availability risks can cause execution disruption, safety risks and higher contingencies.

one-line thesis: NCC withdrew FY26 guidance due to severe execution delays and payment stoppages in Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) projects, causing a 9% YoY revenue decline despite a record INR79.6k cr order book. While JJM payments have recently resumed (INR560 cr received), the resulting working capital strain drove net debt up by INR940 cr YoY, shifting the recovery narrative to H2/FY27 contingent on sustained government cash flows.
financial scorecard: Revenue INR4,900 cr (-9% YoY); EBITDA INR436 cr (8.96% margin, flat YoY); PAT INR122 cr (2.5% margin, down from 3.59%); Order Book INR79,571 cr (+11% YoY); Net Debt INR2,830 cr (up from INR2,344 cr YoY). One-offs: Significant unbilled revenue buildup (INR7,129 cr) due to JJM certification delays; Capex spend on TBM held in CWIP.
guidance: Formal FY26 guidance withdrawn; Management expects Q4 to be 'good' and potentially match prior year (INR5,400 cr) but refuses specific numbers; FY27 capex guided approx INR400 cr.
order book & pipeline: INR79,571 cr (Standalone INR72,748 cr + Subsidiaries INR6,823 cr); Q3 inflows INR12,430 cr; 9M inflows INR22,311 cr; Diversification: Buildings 31%, Transportation 22%, Electrical T&D 18%, Mining 13%, Water & Railway 10%, Others 7%.
segment / subsidiary detail: Buildings segment faced headwinds partly due to JJM overlap; Mining segment driving future capex (INR300-350 cr); Electrical T&D includes smart meter projects; Transportation includes tunnel/coastal road projects now fully mobilized.
growth verticals / optionality: Conversion of INR7,000 cr JJM backlog into revenue as payments normalize; Execution ramp-up of INR28,000 cr orders won in Q4FY25 now cleared for mobilization; Smart meter project commissioning.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin resilient at ~9% despite low volume due to cost rationalization; 79% of contracts have escalation clauses mitigating commodity price risk; Margin pressure from delayed billings impacting PBT conversion.
capex / expansion: FY26 capex revised to INR1,050 cr (from INR750 cr); 9M spend INR265 cr (cash) + INR350 cr (CWIP/TBM); FY27 capex est. INR400 cr (Mining equipment + TBM phases).
capital allocation: Debt used to fund working capital gap from JJM delays and smart meter investments (INR377 cr invested so far); NCCIHL merger completed, consolidating subsidiary accounts; No dividend commentary.
risks & watch-items: Sustained government payment delays (specifically JJM); Right-of-Way (ROW) clearance delays; High working capital days (119 days) straining liquidity; Concentration risk in UP for JJM receivables.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic on cash flow revival but defensive on guidance; Transparent about JJM payment bottlenecks; Emphasized external factors (client payments/ROW) over internal execution failures.
non-obvious takeaways: The debt spike is largely structural/temporary due to CWIP accounting for TBM (not yet depreciating) and bridging finance for JJM until Jan payments hit; Unbilled revenue of INR7.1k cr represents a latent revenue buffer that will flip to P&L upon certification.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delayed payments caused working capital crunch and debt rise | HDFC Bank | beneficiary | Med | Likely lender for the INR865 cr debt increase and working capital limits; benefits from interest income on rising loan book. |

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Buildings segment faced headwinds partly due to JJM overlap; Mining segment driving future capex (INR300-350 cr); Electrical T&D includes smart meter projects; Transportation includes tunnel/coastal road projects now fully mobilized.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Buildings:** Hospitals and medical colleges (e.g. AIIMS), Airports, Sports complexes, Housing projects, IT parks, Industrial and commercial buildings
- **Transportation:** Access-controlled highways, Road EPC projects, Air strips, Metro rail, Tunnelling, Bridges and flyovers
- **Irrigation:** Dams, Reservoirs, Canals, Tunnels, Barrages, Spillways, Aqueducts
- **Railways:** Civil EPC, Track laying, Signalling and telecommunication, Dedicated freight corridors, High-speed rail, Rolling stock and allied systems
- **Water & Environment:** Water supply projects, Treatment plants, Distribution networks, Underground drainage, Sewage treatment plants, Lift irrigation schemes
- **Electrical (T&D):** Transmission and distribution lines, Substations, Project electrification, System improvement projects, Smart meters, Optical fibre
- **Mining:** Mine Developer-cum-Operator activities, Overburden removal, Coal excavation and transportation

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's continued infrastructure investment thrust across public capex, urbanisation, water supply, roads, metro systems, railways, power distribution and digital infrastructure supports medium and long-term demand
- Large government programmes anchor the addressable pipeline: Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 (extended to December 2028, revised outlay `8.69 lakh crore), National Infrastructure Pipeline, PM Gati Shakti, Bharat Mala roads, Railway Modernisation, Metro/RRTS expansion and National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0
- ICRA (March 2026) expects diversified EPC players active in urban infrastructure, irrigation, mining and power — a group the Company's multi-segment platform and limited road-sector concentration positions it within — to grow operating income around 8-10% in FY2026-27 versus road-focused contractors facing pressure from competition and thin order books
- Order book weighted toward Government and Government-agency counterparties reduces counterparty risk
- Infrastructure execution is becoming more complex — larger projects, stringent timelines, higher compliance expectations, and greater technology, safety and sustainability requirements from clients
- Execution pacing during FY26 was affected by extended receivable cycles, approvals, right-of-way constraints and project-specific mobilisation conditions, particularly in water and state-funded segments
- Consolidated order book increased to `83,004 crore as on March 31, 2026 from `71,568 crore in FY25, representing 16% year-on-year growth
- FY26 order inflows of `31,884 crore (including change in scope of work); order execution of `20,447 crore
- Standalone order book stood at `72,259 crore
- Order book composition by vertical: Buildings 27%, Transportation 20%, Mining 17%, Electrical 17%, Water & Railways 12%, Irrigation & Others 7%
- Diversified order book across Buildings, Transportation, Water & Railways, Electrical, Irrigation and Mining is described as reducing concentration risk and providing multi-year execution visibility

capex_expansion.body: As an EPC/construction contractor, NCC's 'expansion' is expressed through the scale and mix of client-awarded projects under execution rather than owned-plant capex. In Water & Environment, ongoing projects include the Multigroup Village Water Supply Scheme Firozabad Pkg-1 (Uttar Pradesh, raw water intake 586 MLD and WTPs of 456 MLD serving ~780 villages), Water Supply Scheme Agra Pkg-1 (17 Clear Water Reservoirs of 14,975 KL capacity serving 899 villages), Patwadh Water Supply Scheme (120 MLD water treatment plant with associated pipelines) and the Kasara Dantiwada Lift Irrigation scheme in Gujarat (MS pipeline exceeding 200 km connecting 159 ponds across 60 villages, irrigating 7,500 hectares). In Irrigation, major FY26 projects include the Barnar Reservoir in Bihar (~2.83 TMC capacity, primarily agricultural/groundwater recharge) and the Palamuru Reservoir in Telangana (part of the Palamuru-Rangaredy Lift Irrigation Scheme, gross capacity 16.4 TMC, with an expansive bund stretching ~15.23 km), plus the Punganur Branch Canal in Rayalseema, Andhra Pradesh. In Electrical (T&D), FY26 major projects span High Voltage 400/220 kV AIS/GIS substations for State DISCOMs in Karnataka and Telangana, distribution-line and system-improvement upgrades across Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Jharkhand, distribution automation and underground cabling for BESCOM in Karnataka, smart prepaid metering for State DISCOMs in North Bihar and Maharashtra, and optical fibre network build-out for BSNL in Madhya Pradesh and Uttarakhand connecting Gram Panchayats and villages.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic on cash flow revival but defensive on guidance; Transparent about JJM payment bottlenecks; Emphasized external factors (client payments/ROW) over internal execution failures.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Multi-disciplinary engineering base across seven infrastructure verticals reduces dependence on any single sector
- Pan-India presence with long-standing relationships with public and private sector clients
- Diversified order book (`83,004 crore consolidated, FY26) balancing sectoral risk
- Project management systems, equipment base and skilled workforce built over four decades of execution experience
- Disciplined bidding and selective project selection prioritising execution capability and revenue visibility over speculative growth

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Sustained government payment delays (specifically JJM); Right-of-Way (ROW) clearance delays; High working capital days (119 days) straining liquidity; Concentration risk in UP for JJM receivables.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The debt spike is largely structural/temporary due to CWIP accounting for TBM (not yet depreciating) and bridging finance for JJM until Jan payments hit; Unbilled revenue of INR7.1k cr represents a latent revenue buffer that will flip to P&L upon certification.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Selective, disciplined bidding — prioritise projects that match execution capability, offer revenue visibility and a balanced risk-return profile, avoiding speculative growth
- Protect project-level economics and margins across market cycles rather than chase scale
- Strengthen working capital management: collections, cash conversion and procurement planning
- Strengthen digital project controls, project monitoring systems and risk-based decision-making
- Maintain a diversified, multi-vertical portfolio (Buildings, Transportation, Water & Environment, Electrical T&D, Irrigation, Railways, Mining) to …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delayed payments caused working capital crunch and debt rise | HDFC Bank | beneficiary | Med | Likely lender for the INR865 cr debt increase and working capital limits; benefits from interest income on rising loan book. |
| Government capex revival in water sector | VA Tech Wabag | beneficiary | Low | Sector peer in water; NCC's resolution of JJM issues signals broader sector payment normalization. |
| Raw material price volatility | JSW Steel | loser | Low | While 79% contracts have escalation clauses, any lag in pass-through or non-covered items impacts EPC margins. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Subsidiary stakes] Ownership disclosed as Pachhwara Coal Mining 51%, NCC Urban Infrastructure 80%, and the two AMI smart meter SPVs 100% each; NCC's investment in NCC Urban held flat at Rs 216 Cr across Q1 FY26, Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27.
- [Execution risk] Management flags that sector execution "continues to be influenced by fund allocation, client approvals, land availability, utility shifting and billing milestones", mitigated through disciplined planning and stakeholder engagement.
- [Recognition] Awards cited include the Golden Hook Award (LISA 2026, MMRDA Metro C-102), ISDA Infracon Platinum (IINA 2026 HSE), MSEDCL certificate for 2.3 mn safe hours on RDSS T-17 and a PWD Assam certificate for 6 mn safe hours.
